items.title: Hard outcomes rarely evaluated
items.whyItMatters: Only a handful of evaluations report death or ICU admission, and the one case-control estimate is imprecise (claim c1).
items.opportunity: Estimate the association with death or ICU admission with enough cases for a useful interval.

items.title: Confounding by indication
items.whyItMatters: Complex patients are enrolled first and the unadjusted association can reverse (claim c2).
items.opportunity: Match on age, sex and calendar time and adjust for prior visits, comorbidity, mental health and housing.

items.title: Time-varying exposure and control sampling
items.whyItMatters: Sampling controls from end-of-follow-up survivors overstates protection (claim c5).
items.opportunity: Use incidence density sampling and measure enrolment before each index date.

items.title: Program intensity differs by site
items.whyItMatters: Community programs use nurses, have different caseloads and enrol later (claim c4).
items.opportunity: If more than one site is included, match controls within site and report site-specific estimates.

items.title: People without a family doctor or stable housing
items.whyItMatters: They carry the highest risk and may be enrolled late or lost from records.
items.opportunity: Report estimates by family doctor attachment and housing status.

errorsFound: The program is monitored by visit counts, which fall after a peak whether or not the program works.
reevaluation: The gaps confirm a matched case-control design with incidence density sampling and careful confounder control; the number of sites is the open choice.
summary: Five gaps: hard outcomes, confounding, control sampling, site differences and equity.
